reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses CALPHAD for phase selection but not for melting properties or DSC integration. E2 notes that CALPHAD predictions for HEAs are challenging even with binary/ternary data, contradicting the premise of reliable prediction. E3 is about phase transformation kinetics in a specific HEA, not about DSC measurement of fusion properties or hybrid method validation. No evidence supports the claimed accuracy or the mediating role of configurational entropy in the hybrid approach.
premises: DSC can reliably measure melting temperature, enthalpy, and entropy of fusion for HEAs
CALPHAD can predict melting and liquid-phase properties for HEAs when binary/ternary data are available
Combining DSC and CALPHAD reduces individual uncertainties and improves accuracy
Configurational entropy mediates the link between atomic mixing and macroscopic phase transitions, captured by both methods
The hybrid approach can achieve ±10–15% accuracy for melting properties across HEA compositions
